localeCode.description: BCP 47 tag used to format dates and plurals in this language.

extDescription.message: See the real TLS certificate of the current site and detect interception by comparing it with independent notaries.

extDescriptionLite.message: See the TLS certificate of the current site as independent notary servers receive it.

unsupportedBody.message: Open a website (http or https) and click the icon again to see its certificate.

loadingReload.message: Reloading the page to read the certificate…

loadingDebuggerBar.message: While the certificate is read, Chrome shows a bar for a few seconds saying SSL Checker is debugging the browser.

externalSkippedInternal.message: Internal site: external sources cannot reach it, so they were not asked.

noSourcesNote.message: Add an external source to compare what your browser receives with what others see.

noSourcesNoteLite.message: This version reads certificates only through external sources. Add one in Options.

askLocalText.message: Reading from your browser is set to on demand. Chrome will show its debugging bar for a few seconds.

probeBlockedText.message: This page blocks the small request used to read the certificate (Content Security Policy). Reloading the page reads it reliably.

verdictConfirmedBody.message: Your browser receives the same certificate the external sources see. Nobody is replacing it on the way.

verdictSameCaBody.message: The external sources receive another certificate from the same authority ($1). That is normal for CDNs and during certificate rotation.

verdictPublicBody.message: Chrome confirmed the certificate is in the public Certificate Transparency logs, so no local proxy or antivirus made it. Add external sources to cross-check it.

verdictPublicBodyNoAnswer.message: Chrome confirmed the certificate is in the public Certificate Transparency logs, so no local proxy or antivirus made it. The external sources did not answer.

verdictPrivateCaTitle.message: Not confirmed as a public certificate

verdictPrivateCaBody.message: Chrome did not confirm that this certificate, issued by $1, is in the public Certificate Transparency logs. That happens when it comes from a locally installed authority (company network, antivirus, internal server) or when the browser's list of CT logs is out of date. Add external sources to find out whether the connection is intercepted.

verdictInterceptedBody.message: Your browser receives a certificate issued by $1, but external sources see one issued by $2, and Chrome did not confirm yours is publicly logged. Most likely something between you and the site (company proxy, antivirus or something else) decrypts and re-signs the traffic.

verdictSplitBody.message: Same certificate as yours: $1. A different one, issued by $2: $3. Either your connection is intercepted and the matching sources share your network, or the network of the other sources is intercepted.

verdictInterceptorBody.message: The certificate is issued by $1 and is not in the public Certificate Transparency logs, which is how HTTPS inspection products work.

verdictConflictBody.message: Your browser and the external sources see different public certificates (yours issued by $1, theirs by $2). Sites behind several CDNs do this, but it is worth a look.

verdictExternalBody.message: Reading from your browser is off, so an interception on your network cannot be detected. This is what the sources see.

verdictExternalBodyAsk.message: Read the certificate from your browser to compare it with what the sources see.

verdictExternalBodyLocalFailed.message: The certificate could not be read from your browser, so an interception on your network cannot be ruled out. This is what the sources see.

verdictExternalBodyLite.message: This version cannot read the certificate from your browser, so an interception on your network cannot be detected. This is what the sources see.

verdictExternalDisagreeBody.message: The external sources see different certificates from one another.

verdictHttpBody.message: This page loaded over plain HTTP, so anyone on the network can read or change it. No certificate protects it.

verdictHttpBodyWithCert.message: This page loaded over plain HTTP, so anyone on the network can read or change it. Below is the certificate the server offers on HTTPS (port 443).

verdictNoSourcesBody.message: Turn on reading from the browser or add an external source in Options.

verdictNoSourcesLite.message: Add an external source in Options to see this site's certificate.

verdictNoSourcesLocalFailed.message: The certificate could not be read from your browser and no external source answered.

verdictInternalBody.message: External sources cannot reach internal sites, and the certificate was not read from your browser.

verdictAllSourcesFailed.message: None of the external sources answered. Check them in Options.

verdictAskBody.message: Reading from the browser is set to on demand.

warnNotYetValid.message: The certificate is not valid yet.

warnWeakSignature.message: The chain uses a weak signature (SHA-1 or MD5).

warnWeakKey.message: The RSA key has only $1 bits.

warnNotaryUntrusted.message: $1 does not trust the certificate it sees: $2.

warnNotPubliclyLogged.message: Chrome did not confirm that this certificate is publicly logged.

warnSomeSourcesDiffer.message: Different certificate seen by $1 (issued by $2). Yours is publicly logged, so the difference is probably on their side.

localErr_restrictedPage.message: Chrome does not allow reading this page (internal page, error page or another extension's page).

localErr_blockedByPolicy.message: Your organization's policy blocks reading certificates from the browser.

localErr_probeBlocked.message: The page blocked the request used to read the certificate.

localErr_reloadFailed.message: The page did not finish loading in time.

localErr_canceledByUser.message: Reading was cancelled from Chrome's debugging bar.

localErr_navigated.message: The tab moved to another site. Check again.

localErr_noCertificate.message: Chrome did not return a certificate for this page.

localErr_notHttps.message: The page is not served over HTTPS.

localErr_alreadyAttached.message: Another debugger is attached to this tab.

notaryErr_network.message: Could not reach the source (network error or missing CORS headers).

notaryErr_rateLimited.message: Too many requests; the source asks to slow down.

notaryErr_badResponse.message: The source sent an invalid answer.

notaryErr_badCertificate.message: The source sent an unreadable certificate.

notaryErr_forbiddenTarget.message: The source refuses this address (private or reserved).

notaryErr_forbiddenPort.message: The source does not check this port.

notaryErr_dnsFailed.message: The source could not resolve the site's name.

notaryErr_connectFailed.message: The source could not connect to the site.

notaryErr_tlsFailed.message: The TLS handshake failed at the source.

notaryErr_busy.message: The source is busy; try again shortly.

notaryErr_badRequest.message: The source did not understand the request.

historyFirst.message: First check of this site. From now on SSL Checker remembers that its certificate comes from $1.

historyKnown.message: Same certificate authority as in your earlier checks: $1, $2 since $3.

historyLearned.message: From now on SSL Checker also remembers $1 for this site.

historyChangedBefore.message: Until now: $1, $2, the last one on $3.

historySameName.message: The authority has the same name as before, but it signs with a key never seen for this site.

historyTrusted.message: $1 is now trusted for this site.

historyForgotten.message: This site was forgotten. The next check starts its history again.

verdictCaChangedBody.message: In your earlier checks this site always had a public certificate from $1. Now your browser receives one from $2 that is not publicly logged. Most likely something between you and the site intercepts the connection.

verdictCaChangedSameNameBody.message: The certificate claims to come from $1, as before, but it is signed with a key never seen for this site and it is not publicly logged. Most likely something between you and the site intercepts the connection.

warnCaChanged.message: This site's certificate authority changed: $1 before, $2 now.

warnCaChangedSameName.message: The certificate claims to come from $1, as before, but it is signed with a key never seen for this site.

warnCaChangedPublic.message: This site switched from $1 to $2. The new certificate is publicly logged.

warnCaChangedNowPublic.message: Earlier checks of this site went through $1, an authority installed on this computer or network (for example a company proxy). Now the certificate is public.

optMemoryIntro.message: When the certificate is read from your browser, SSL Checker remembers which authority issued it for each site you check, and warns you when a site you know suddenly arrives with a different one. Everything stays on this device.

fieldMemoryEnabled.message: Remember the certificate authority of the sites I check

optMemoryHelp.message: Turning it off stops recording. To delete what is already stored, use Forget all sites.

optionsIntro.message: Choose how the certificate is read and which external sources it is compared with.

optLocalIntro.message: This shows the exact certificate your browser received, so an interception on your network can be detected. Chrome has no dedicated API for it, so the extension attaches its debugger to the tab for about a second; meanwhile Chrome shows a bar saying SSL Checker is debugging the browser.

optLocalUnavailable.message: This version of SSL Checker does not include the debugger permission, so certificates are read only through external sources.

modeAlwaysHelp.message: Read the certificate whenever you open SSL Checker.

modeAskHelp.message: Show the external results first; read from the browser only when you click.

modeNeverHelp.message: Use only external sources. The debugging bar never appears.

optSourcesIntro.message: Each source is a notary server that connects to the site from elsewhere on the internet and reports the certificate it receives. Only the site's host name and port are sent to it.

fieldUrlHelp.message: HTTPS address of the notary. Put {host} and {port} in it if the server expects them in the path; otherwise they are added as ?host=…&port=…

fieldTokenHelp.message: Sent as Authorization: Bearer. Stored only on this device.

testOk.message: Works: it sees example.com's certificate issued by $1, from $2, in $3 ms.

endpointErrorCredentialsInUrl.message: Do not put a user name or password in the address; use the token field.

endpointErrorFragment.message: Remove the # part from the address.

endpointErrorPlaceholderInHost.message: {host} can appear only in the path or the query of the address.

endpointErrorHttps.message: The address must use HTTPS (plain HTTP is allowed only for localhost).

endpointErrorDuplicate.message: This source is already in the list.

endpointErrorToken.message: The token can contain only visible ASCII characters.

optProtocolIntro.message: Any server that answers this request can be a source. The reference implementation is a single Node.js file you can run on your own server.

optProtocolErrors.message: On errors, answer with a 4xx or 5xx status and {"version": 1, "error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}. The extension holds no host permissions, so the server must send CORS headers.
